Commentary.Commentary: 161 to win then. What do you reckon? Going by Mavuta's confidence, Zimbabwe should look at this as a great chance to beat South Africa. They have chased down totals of 160 or more in T20Is just thrice before. Could this be their fourth? On the flip side, looking at how the Zimbabwean spinners bowled, Tahir and Shamsi will be looking to have a party. Stay tuned for the run chase.

Talk about Mavuta and here he is, on the sidelines. Says that he was just trying to bowl wicket-to-wicket and just add some variety to that. Adds he took his time ball by ball and it paid off. States that he took the wind factor into account and decided to go about things accordingly. Informs that he was mentally prepared for this contest and is happy he could do well. Feels the wicket is a good one for batting and backs his boys to get the job done.

A story of three bowlers tells you Zimbabwe's bowling. Chris Mpofu was really poor in the field but with the ball, he was superb. His final over was tremendous, going for just 4 and his 2/24 simply stands out. Brandon Mavuta was the pick of the bowlers in my opinion. He struck on his first ball and did not pick any wicket further but with 10 dots and just 1 boundary, his 1/19 kept South Africa quiet. He found an able partner in Sean Williams who went for just 28 in 4 overs.

Talk about the debutant, Rassie van der Dussen - how well did he play? You never know - this innings could be the difference between victory and defeat. He took his time early on, happy to play second fiddle to his skipper but then took control after seeing Miller struggle. 56 from just 44 balls with 5 fours and a six. Had he stayed on for some more time, the Proteas could have reached 175-180.

Mavuta struck first ball, getting rid of Faf and that stalled the scoring. The Proteas could manage just 65 runs in the next 9 overs and even though no wicket fell, the batsmen could not quite make runs freely. The pressure was telling big time on David Miller and had it not been for the debutant, Rassie van der Dussen, who took it upon himself to try and bat for as long as possible, the Proteas would not have even reached 150.

South Africa, without a doubt have fallen at least 20 runs short of what they would have looked for. They lost their openers cheaply and then captain Faf du Plessis came out all guns blazing. With the Powerplay score reading 52/2, the hosts were back on track but then came the leggie, Brandon Mavuta.
Superb bowling from Zimbabwe. Could have been even better had they fielded well but they will take 160 any day. Now, if they bat sensibly, they can think about going 1-0 up.
Full and outside off, Phehlukwayo gets down and sweeps it through mid-wicket for a couple. Just 4 runs from the final over and Mpofu finishes with figures of 4-0-24-2! ZIMBABWE NEED 161 TO WIN.
Lovely bowling. One more delivered from the back of the hand, a short one at that, AP leaps and attempts the upper cut but misses.
Another dot. A slower one, outside off, Andile looks to push it to the off side but is beaten.
The ball has struck the batsman hard on his hand. One run added to the total. Leg bye given by the umpire.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. One run added to the total.
Full and wide outside off, Phehlukwayo lets it go, thinking it will be a wide but the ball is inside the line.
Junior Dala walks in.

OUT! That is a blinder! Jonker cannot believe it. But he has to go. Full and outside off, Christiaan crashes this over cover but at the last moment, Hamilton Masakadza flies to his right and takes a stunner! They check for the overstepping but Jarvis is just about fine. Ends his spell with figures of 4-0-37-3.
The batsman has done well to keep that yorker at bay.
SIX! THRASH! No short stuff please. It is a long hop which just sits up and asks to be hit. Jonker obliges and as soon as the ball is pitched, he swivels and sends it over deep mid-wicket.
This time he gets it past cover for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
A yorker outside off, Phehlukwayo looks to push it away but misses.
Andile Phehlukwayo walks in at number 7, replacing van der Dussen.

OUT! The debutant departs. A slower ball, outside off, van der Dussen swings hard but early. Gets a top edge which goes only as far as cover. Simple catch for Hamilton Masakadza. A fine 56 from the debutant. Could have seen Zimbabwe on top had this bloke not stood out for so long.
FIVE WIDES! Misfired. Full and down the leg side, van der Dussen misses his flick and poor Taylor behind is blinded. No chance to stop that.
Pushes this through mid on for a couple.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Down the leg side, helped fine for a single.
The batsman goes for the hook but misses the line of the delivery.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. A direct hit by the fielder but the batsman makes it home. They pick up a single.
Christiaan Jonker walks in at number 6, replacing Miller. Meanwhile, Chris Mpofu is back on. 2-0-11-1 so far.

OUT! Taken this time! Miller's struggle ends. Full and on middle, Miller comes down the track and skies it high in the air. Williams comes running in and takes it nicely at long on. End of the 87-run stand.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

CATCH TAKEN BUT IT IS A SIX! Poor luck for Tarisai Musakanda. Miller comes down the track and hits it high in the air. He miscues it and Musakanda gets ready for the catch at the long off fence. However, when he leaps for the catch and then takes it, his first landing is on the ropes. Does not even have time to throw the ball.
Banged short, pulled towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! HALF CENTURY ON DEBUT! Just the third South African after Graeme Smith and Rilee Roussouw to achieve this feat. Gets to the landmark with a bludgeon past the bowler, down the ground, splitting long on and long off.
FOUR! A short ball, on the pads, pulled past Mpofu at short fine leg for a boundary!
Kyle Jarvis is back on. 2-0-15-1 so far.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it. One run added to the total. Not a bad outing for Williams with the ball. 4-0-28-0 tonight.

Close call! The arm ball, around middle and leg, van der Dussen looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. Zimbabwe appeal but that seemed to be going down leg. Meanwhile, Miller initially wants a single but then sees his partner is not looking at him. Aborts the thought.
Full on middle, hit powerfully down to long on for a run.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Nice shot. Full on middle, van der Dussen skips down the track and blasts it down the ground towards long on for a boundary.
Full and outside leg, reverse swept straight to point.
Now he looks to play the conventional sweep but misses again. Is hit on the pads and Mavuta appeals but in vain. Excellent spell from the leggie - 4-0-19-1.
Floated around middle and leg, Miller looks to play the reverse sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
On middle and leg, flicked through the leg side for one.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Brandon Mavuta is back on. His final over. 3-0-15-1 so far.
Full and down the leg side, pushed towards long on for one. 11 from the over, 22 from the last 2!
Full and outside off, pushed wide of the bowler towards long off for a run.
Full and outside off, driven wide of long off for a couple.
Down the leg side, helped towards fine leg for a single.
SIX! TAKE THAT! Full and outside off, Miller gets down and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a biggie!
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads.
Sean Williams gets a change of ends.

FOUR! 50-STAND IS UP IN 41 BALLS. Dropped short, around off, van der Dussen goes back and drags his pull through square leg for a boundary! 100 IS UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA AS WELL. 7 overs left. Can they get to 190?
Misses out. Comes down the track and blasts it, but straight to long off. Just a run.
A low full toss outside off, David squeezes it straight to Chris Mpofu at backward point who fumbles a straightforward chance and concedes a couple.
Much slower this time, tossed up at 88 kph. On the pads, flicked towards deep mid-wicket for a couple.
WIDE. Quicker one, 100 KPH, fired down the leg side. Miller does not even move a muscle.
Dragged short, pulled towards deep mid-wicket for a single. The stand is now worth 40 from 37 balls.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Tendai Chisoro is back on. 2-0-26-0 so far.
On middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket for a run. Just 3 from that over. Brilliant bowling.
Outside off, punched behind point for a quick single. Might have been a run out chance had Kyle Jarvis picked it up cleanly running to his left from backward point but he fumbles.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover.
Fires this on off stump, van der Dussen perhaps makes a late call to play his shot. Just about gets his bat down in time to play the googly through mid-wicket for a single.
And again. Same shot, same result.
Full and around middle, reverse swept straight to point.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.

SAFE. Big opportunity missed by Zimbabwe. Not the run out, but the catch. Full and outside off, Miller comes down the track and looks to go over the leg side but does not get to that at all. He gets a massive leading edge but neither backward point, nor sweeper cover see it. They do not hear Brendan Taylor's shouts either. In the end, the ball drops safely. Miller returns for the second and the throw comes in at his end. It is a good one and he dives, with the run out appeal referred upstairs. Replays show that he is home though.
Run out chance! Is Miller gone?
This is on middle, van der Dussen looks to play the reverse sweep but mistimes it towards cover. A run taken.
Fired outside leg, flicked towards deep square leg for a single.
Full and around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single. 82/3 at the halfway mark. Is 200 still on?
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side. They pick up a single.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover who misfields and concedes a single.

FOUR! That has gone like a tracer bullet! Fractionally short in length, around middle and leg, Miller swivels and plays a pull shot. There is a man in the deep, at square leg and he has to move just a couple of paces. But he cannot even get to it. It is so powerfully struck. In the end, the fielder dives, but in vain. Miller moves to 11 from 11 balls.
Comes down the track and works it wide of long on for a couple. The stand is now worth 21 from 18 balls.
Chamu Chibhabha to bowl now. Sixth bowler in the 10th over.
A short ball, down the leg side, Rassie looks to pull but is unable to connect. The ball goes off his pads down the leg side and a couple of leg byes are taken.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers who dives to his right and parries it to long off. Two runs taken.
A touch short, around leg, punched down to long on for one.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Tossed up outside off, pushed past the diving bowler towards long off for a run.
The googly outside off, short in length, crunched straight to sweeper cover for a single.
Fired on the pads, flicked towards deep square leg for a single.
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. They pick up a single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. Two runs added to the total.
The batsman dances down the track. They pick up a single.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Comes down the track, is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and misses the ball. Is hit on the pads. That nearly went through.
Sean Williams into the attack. Another spinner.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. Good effort by the fielder to ensure the ball doesn't cross the line. They manage to come back for the second.
Full and on middle, there comes the reverse sweep and it is hit towards point where it is fielded well.

FOUR! That should have been stopped though. Full and outside off, Rassie powers a cover drive. It is a full-blooded shot, but slightly to the right of the fielder in the circle. He gets down but is late and the ball goes through.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Full and on the pads, flicked straight to square leg.
David Miller walks in at number 5, replacing his skipper.

OUT! The leggie strikes first ball! MAIDEN T20I WICKET FOR BRANDON MAVUTA. Not a bad scalp to get, eh? Tossed up outside off, Faf dances down the track and straightaway looks to take the leggie on. He aims to get it over extra cover but this time Zimbabwe have outsmarted him. They have seen him go inside out during the Powerplay and immediately kept a man in the deep once the fielding restrictions were lifted. Faf does not count for that. Hits it straight down the throat of Tendai Chisoro who makes no mistake. Can Zimbabwe pile on some pressure now?
A leggie now. Brandon Mavuta introduced to bowl.

Good bowling. Sees Faf advancing and slows the pace down. The skipper looks to force it through the off side but gets a thick inside edge which goes past the leg stump towards short fine leg. A single taken. 52/2 in the Powerplay.
Outside off, played towards short third man. Someone wants the single, someone says 'NO! NO!' Eventually, the pair agrees to the second piece of communication and it is a dot ball.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single. The stand moves to 40 from 23 balls.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
SIX! Now the debutant gets going! A length ball, on the pads, van der Dussen gets across and flicks it powerfully. It goes all the way over backward square leg!
FOUR! Terrific batting again. Full and outside off, du Plessis comes down the track and whips it over mid on and gets a boundary! 14 from the over!
Kyle Jarvis is back for his second over. Change of ends for him. Meanwhile, there seems to be an issue with the Zing bails. One of them has stopped working. Gets replaced.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Super shot. Faf du Plessis is not giving an inch. Once more he skips out of his crease, gets close to the pitch and lifts it over covers to find the fence.
Fuller outside off, driven to covers.
WIDE. Down the leg side, expecting the batsman to move to the leg side but Faf stays where he is and lets it go.
Comes down the track now but the ball is very straight and fast. He is forced to defend.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

OUTSIDE EDGE, FOUR! Faf continues to go for runs. Full and wide outside off, du Plessis backs away to the leg side and then reaches out for the shot, aiming to go inside out. However, unlike last time, where he got a biggie, he gets an outside edge this time, which flies over backward point. Makes it to the fence behind.
Outside off, RvdD looks to pull but misses.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Another short ball, outside off, Rassie looks to hook but is beaten by pace.
Short and outside off, cut straight to cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle and leg, van der Dussen flicks it through mid-wicket, takes the single, notices that the fielder is lazy in attacking the ball and hares back for the second.

SIX! Brilliant batting! Faf is not going to be bogged down by the wickets falling around him. Tossed up outside off, the skipper backs away to the leg side, creates a little bit of room for him and boom. Lofts this full ball outside off over cover. 12 from the over, both in maximums.
Outside off, a tad short, Faf goes back and punches it straight to cover.
SIX! Fine shot. Tossed up outside off, du Plessis comes down the track and sends it sailing over wide long on!
Full and straight, hit back to the bowler.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
Full and outside off, that is a dart, driven straight to cover.
Tendai Chisoro to bowl his left-arm spin.

IN THE AIR, SAFE! Nervy moments for Faf and South Africa. A length ball outside off, FdP looks to chip it over mid off but there is no timing, because he is beaten by lack of pace. He mistimes it in the air but luckily for him, the ball lands right in between mid on and mid off! A single is taken.
INSIDE EDGE MISSES THE STUMPS! Things are happening. Full and outside off, Faf is a bit lazy in getting forward, looks to push but gets a thick inside edge which just misses the sticks!
FOUR! Lucky one!  A short ball, around middle, du Plessis looks to pull but is cramped for room. He gets a top edge which goes over short fine leg!
Another debutant is in. Rassie van der Dussen walks in at number 4, replacing de Kock.

OUT! Both the openers are gone now. What a start from Zimbabwe! A short ball, around middle, but it is slower in pace. De Kock does not read that and goes for the pull quickly. Gets a top edge which goes high in the air. Chamu Chibhabha keeps his eyes on the ball and takes it easily at deep mid-wicket. Not a great comeback for QdK.
ALMOST! Around off, Quinton looks to defend but the ball takes the bottom edge and rolls behind, just about missing the off stump!

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for South Africa. A length ball outside off, de Kock steers it behind point. Jarvis gives it a good chase from third man to his left, dives but cannot prevent the boundary.
Chris Mpofu to share the new ball with Jarvis.
FOUR! Outstanding timing! The ball is full and too straight. The skipper walks into the shot, gets across and flicks it easily through mid-wicket. The ball races away!
Skipper Faf du Plessis strides in at number 3, much earlier than he would have anticipated.

OUT! And now, the debutant is going back! A decent nut from Jarvis. He lands it on a length, slightly outside off and Cloete has a feel for it. But at the last moment, the ball moves away and takes the outside edge. Goes straight to Hamilton Masakadza at first slip who cups it easily to his right. Not a great debut with the bat then, for Cloete.
A length ball outside off, Gihahn plays at it and gets a thick outside edge, behind point towards third man. It almost meets the fence but is saved in the end. Two runs to get the debutant going.
A short ball, around middle and leg, Cloete sways away.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
On a length around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
We are all ready to begin then. Quinton de Kock and Gihahn Cloete are the openers for the home side. Kyle Jarvis has the new ball in his hand. De Kock to face. Here we go!

A few debutants in this game. Gihahn Cloete and Rassie van der Dussen are given opportunities by the Proteas. The Proteas are going in with two spinners in Tahir and Shamsi, while the seamers are Phehlukwayo, Dala and Ngidi. As far as Zimbabwe are concerned, they have just the one spinner in Chisoro. Interesting tactics.
TOSS - Faf du Plessis has won the spin of the coin. SOUTH AFRICA HAVE ELECTED TO BAT.

We are all set for the T20I series to begin. With India crushing Windies and Pakistan dominating Australia, a South Africa-Zimbabwe clash does not provide too much expectations. However, since the format is T20, we can hope that Zimbabwe can do better than what they did in the ODIs. Hello and a warm welcome to the first T20I of the 3-match series between South Africa and Zimbabwe in East London.
